source.title: Post mortem on the Cloudflare Control Plane and Analytics Outage
source.source_type: operator first-party postmortem; contains explicitly labeled informed speculation about the colocation provider

observed_symptoms.fact: Control plane (dashboard, APIs) and analytics/logging services went down; two routers connecting the Portland PDX-04 facility went offline at 11:44 and could not be reached directly or out of band.
Most of the control plane was restored at the disaster recovery facility by 17:57 on Nov 2; raw log services were unavailable for most customers for the whole incident.
observed_symptoms.measurement: control plane mostly restored ~6 h; logs down ~40 h

observed_symptoms.fact: Network and security services kept working and customer traffic was not impacted, though customers could not make changes for periods.
Turning up services on the disaster recovery site caused a thundering-herd of API calls that required rate limiting.
Some datasets not replicated to the EU have persistent gaps; log push logs for most of the event were not processed and cannot be recovered.

confirmed_root_cause.mechanism: Total power loss at the Flexential PDX-04 data center took out Cloudflare's largest analytics cluster, more than a third of its high-availability control-plane machines, and the default home of services not yet on the HA cluster. The outage was amplified by Cloudflare design gaps: some services supposedly on the HA cluster depended on Kafka and ClickHouse that existed only in PDX-04, logging was intentionally outside the HA cluster, some newer products were not integrated with HA or tested on DR, and the entire PDX-04 facility had never been tested offline.
confirmed_elements: Power was lost at PDX-04 and the UPS batteries began failing after about 4 minutes instead of the expected 10
Flexential did not tell Cloudflare it had moved to generators; first provider message came at 12:28
Kafka and ClickHouse were only in PDX-04 yet HA services depended on them
Disaster recovery sites do not support some log processing services
Flexential's circuit breakers for Cloudflare's circuits were found faulty during power-up
contributing_factors: Newer products were not required to use the HA cluster before general availability
Too many services depend on core facilities
Full PDX-04 failure had not been tested
unconfirmed_or_speculative: Why Flexential ran utility and generator power together and whether its grid-support program was involved
That a ground fault on a utility transformer at about 11:40 tripped the generators
Whether the faulty breakers failed because of the incident

investigation_evidence.evidence: Two routers connecting the facility went offline; direct and out-of-band management unreachable.
Cloudflare's own equipment began failing about 4 minutes after power loss, showing UPS batteries failed early.
First notice from Flexential reported a power issue.
Services in the HA cluster were found to depend on Kafka and ClickHouse only in PDX-04.
Prior failure tests had removed other facilities and the HA part of PDX-04 but never all of PDX-04.

recovery_actions.action: Decided to fail over the affected control plane to disaster recovery sites in Europe; first services were up at 13:43.
recovery_actions.why: Provider could not give a restoration time.

recovery_actions.action: Implemented rate limits to control the thundering herd.
recovery_actions.why: API calls that had been failing overwhelmed turned-up services.

recovery_actions.action: Worked two tracks for products that did not start on DR: re-implement on DR and migrate to the HA cluster.
recovery_actions.why: Newer products lacked tested DR procedures.

recovery_actions.action: Flexential replaced the failed breakers, restored both utility feeds and confirmed clean power.
Full bootstrap of PDX-04: network gear, configuration management servers (about 3 hours), then rebuild of servers at 10 minutes to 2 hours each, partly in sequence.
recovery_actions.why: State was unknown after multiple power cycles.

recovery_verification.method: Services moved to DR were stable and most customers no longer directly impacted.
Services fully restored for all customers.

acceptable_alternatives.description: Fail over control plane to DR sites while PDX-04 is down (partial recovery; logs and analytics remain down)
Restore PDX-04 power and bootstrap the facility (only path that restored all services)
acceptable_alternatives.basis: R4, R5, V3; power repair was done by the provider

acceptable_alternatives.description: Enable DR for both control plane and analytics so everything recovers during the outage
acceptable_alternatives.basis: DR sites do not support some log processing and Kafka/ClickHouse were only in PDX-04

acceptable_alternatives.description: Move services to the HA cluster; stronger chaos tests; Code Orange reliability focus

not_stated_in_source: Any repair cost or relative effort
Verified root cause of the power chain of events (explicitly speculative)

fixture_alignment.hypothesis_alignment: H03 (primary power loss plus incomplete failover readiness) matches; confirmed power loss is separate from the speculative upstream cause.

A01.note: DR control-plane failover restored most of the control plane while analytics stayed down.

A02.note: Analytics replica alone is not described; analytics failover was not available on DR.

A03.note: Restore primary-site power; done by the provider and followed by about 30 more hours of rebuild.

A04.note: The source says analytics and log processing could not run on DR.
